subject: Grandfathering SLA tiers + accelerated oncall add-on — follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@cloudweave.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@cloudweave.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA tiers and support packaging questions

Thanks for the slides this morning, Jordan — two quick items on our side as we prepare legal/procurement: 1) CloudWeave has existing customers covered under your prior 99.9% uptime table; we need clarity on whether they'd be "grandfathered" or moved to the new tiers if we sign a three-year commit; 2) procurement asked whether you can provide a short add-on for an "accelerated oncall" option (1-hour response, 24/7) that can be toggled per environment and billed as a seat credit.

Can you share a clear pricing delta and how credits will be consumed across multi-region failovers? Also loop legal if possible — we may ask for a 60-day transition clause.

Appreciate it,
Alex Torres
Head of Platform Ops, CloudWeave
alex.torres@cloudweave.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@cloudweave.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA tiers and support packaging questions

Alex — thanks, good questions. Short answers up front: we can grandfather existing customers on the prior SLA table for up to 24 months from signature (with an opt-in to migrate earlier), and yes — we can create a togglable accelerated-oncall add-on billed via seat credits.

I've attached a short draft that shows the grandfathering window, pricing deltas for the accelerated-oncall (list price + volume discounts), and an example commit grid that demonstrates credit consumption during a cross-region failover. Key highlights:
- Grandfathering: 12 months standard, can extend to 24 months at a 10% surcharge to the overall commit (one-time election at signing).
- Accelerated-oncall add-on: +40% on top of the base premium SLA line for 1h response 24/7; seat-credit billing at 0.6 credits/hour per seat during active incident windows (we bill daily increments).
- Multi-region failover: credits consume from primary region pool first; if exhausted, fallback from global reserve (we show a simulated waterfall in the attached grid).

I'll pull in legal and pricing to finalize language. Can Kimberly/Karthik confirm whether the 40% uplift and the 0.6 credit rate are feasible from an ops-cost perspective?

--
Jordan Blake
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0124

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T14:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA tiers and support packaging questions

Jordan / team — ran the high-level math with infra/ops. Notes:
- 40% uplift is aggressive but acceptable for a pilot at CloudWeave scale if we tie it to a three-year commit and minimum MRR threshold. Ops wants a hard cap on concurrent accelerated seats per account to avoid unbounded oncall exposure; recommend a capacity holdback of 15% at initial roll-out.
- 0.6 credits/hour aligns with our current incident average for a single responder; recommend we keep daily billing but include an incident-minimum of 2 hours for seat credit consumption accounting.
- Grandfathering: we can support 12 months at no charge, 24 months with a 10% surcharge as Jordan suggested, but legal requests a short clause enumerating which customers are eligible (must be identified by account id).

Action items for Jordan: confirm ask from procurement on the 60-day transition clause and whether CloudWeave needs an explicit opt-in form for legacy customers. I'll prepare a one-page ops note to attach to the SOW outlining capacity holdback and incident-minimum.

Kimberly Park
VP, Customer Reliability Programs
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@cloudweave.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@cloudweave.com>, procurement@cloudweave.com
Date: 2026-11-23T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Grandfathering SLA tiers + accelerated oncall add-on — follow-up

Thanks Jordan and Kimberly — quick clarifications from procurement/legal:
1) The 60-day transition clause would need to include a rollback mechanism: if CloudWeave chooses to reclassify a workload back to legacy tier within the 60 days, charges should be prorated and we need a clear audit trail.
2) For grandfathering eligibility, we can provide a CSV of account ids; legal wants the 24-month surcharge to be mutually agreed and not unilateral.
3) Regarding capacity holdback: procurement asks for a small discount (5% off the accelerated-oncall uplift) if we accept a two-year minimum instead of three.

Can you send an updated SOW + price table reflecting: 12m free grandfathering / 24m at 10% surcharge (mutual opt-in), accelerated-oncall +40% (or +35% if 2-year commit), capacity holdback 15%, incident-minimum 2 hours, and explicit proration language for the 60-day transition?

Maya
Senior Procurement Manager, CloudWeave

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@cloudweave.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@cloudweave.com>, procurement@cloudweave.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Grandfathering SLA tiers + accelerated oncall add-on — follow-up

Team — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is an updated SOW and pricing grid (SLA_Grandfathering_Draft_v1.pdf and Commit_and_Credit_Grid_CloudWeave.xlsx). Summary of changes:
- Grandfathering: 12m at no cost; 24m available with a mutual opt-in and 10% surcharge on the signed commit. We will require CloudWeave to provide the CSV of account ids at signing; Redwood will perform a verification run within 7 business days.
- Accelerated-oncall: base uplift +40%. If CloudWeave elects a 2-year minimum commit (vs 3-year), uplift is reduced to +35% with the same seat-credit math (0.6 credits/hr, 2-hour incident minimum).
- Capacity holdback: 15% initial cap. Redwood will provide a monthly utilization report and a mechanism to request temporary increases (subject to availability).
- 60-day transition clause: proration allowed; rollback to legacy tier triggers a credit equal to the unused portion of the accelerated-oncall uplift pro-rated to the day. All changes require written confirmation; audit logs will be provided for credit reconciliation.

Next steps: if CloudWeave agrees in principle, I'll route this to Legal and Procurement for signature and ask Pricing to confirm final numbers in the attached excel. Please respond with any redlines by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-29).

Cheers,
Jordan
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
